title: Emile Barnes and the early band with Steve Angrum and Teat
summary: Dick Allen mentions seeing Emile Barnes; Thomas says he took Emile on around 1941 after Steve Angrum left, and that the band in the photograph predated the Depression.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Tom, I'll tell you, I'm going to start the interview a little later. I saw a friend of yours today, Emile Barnes. We just saw him this morning. Yeah. Man, I seen Emile Barnes. When did you first start working with him? Can you remember?

Man, way back in, let me see. 19 what? 19... Run... Run 41, something like that. Uh-huh. Because I had that boy, what you call, playing with me, and then Steve, you know, Steve Angle. Steve Angle? Yeah, he was playing with me first head out there, you know what I mean? Yeah. And now that Steve, he pulled out and went, you know, so I got Emile to play.
That's the band on that photograph from that magazine. Yeah, yeah. Yeah, with T. Ruchon over there. Yeah, yeah. What time? Was that before World War II? Oh no.
Yeah. Before? No. Yeah, it was before, yeah. Yeah, it was. Was it before the Depression? Yeah, yeah, yeah, before the Depression. Sure, we used to play on the lake and everywhere.
Oh yeah, before they tore the lake then?
Yeah, sure, before the... Before they tore the millimum. What was the name of that band?
You remember? My band? Was that your band? Yeah. You run it?
